symptom: A project becomes unopenable after an mxcli write — Studio Pro / `mx check` fails with `System.Collections.Generic.KeyNotFoundException: The given key '<guid>' was not present in the dictionary` at `StreamingBsonUnitReader.ResolvePostponedProperties`. `mx check` on the *previous* revision is clean, and only some document types break (microflows/nanoflows yes, pages/navigation no)
cause: An element's `$ID` was rewritten without rewriting the references that point at it. Mendix's loader defers reference resolution and then looks the target up by ID, so a pointer holding a discarded ID is a dangling reference. Hit by `element.PreserveIDs` (reverted in `f1371f71`), which recursed through `ChildProperty`/`ChildListProperty` and called `SetID`, but **pointers are not child properties** — `Microflows$SequenceFlow.OriginPointer`/`DestinationPointer` are primitive properties holding an `element.ID` (`modelsdk/gen/microflows/types.go` `InitFromRaw`), invisible to a child-walk
insight: **Never rewrite an element ID without rewriting every reference to it in the same pass.** `ResolvePostponedProperties` in the stack trace means exactly this: a stored ID has no owner. The document types that survive are the ones with few internal cross-references (a page's widget tree is containment, a microflow's is a graph), so **"pages are fine" is not evidence the approach is safe**. Better than a fixup pass: seed the rebuild with the stored IDs so pointers are computed correctly from the start. **Verification lesson**: the local test project had entities, an association, an enumeration and constants but *no microflow*, so `mx check` reported 0 errors on a model that could not exercise the bug — a green `mx check` only covers the constructs the fixture actually contains. `make test-integration` (which needs mxbuild, ~20 min) caught it via `TestMxCheck_DoctypeScripts`; unit tests alone did not. Run it before claiming a write-path change is safe
